title: Excellence of strict local rings of finite-type field algebras
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and $B$ a finitely generated commutative $k$-algebra (a quotient of a polynomial ring in finitely many variables). Let $\mathfrak p$ be a prime ideal of $B$, put $L=B_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], choose a separable closure $K$ of its residue field, and let $C=L^{\mathrm{sh}}$ be a strict henselization relative to $K$ [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization]. Then $L$, $C$, and every quotient $C/I$ by an ideal $I$ are excellent. In particular $C$ and $C/\sqrt{(0)}$ are Noetherian.

Here a ring $D$ is excellent [def-exc-excellent-ring] if it is a Noetherian G-ring [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], its regular locus is open after every finite-type algebra extension, and it is universally catenary. More explicitly, for every finitely generated $D$-algebra $E$, the subset of $\operatorname{Spec}E$ consisting of primes $\mathfrak q$ for which $E_{\mathfrak q}$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] is open, and for any two primes $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak r$ of $E$ all saturated chains of primes between them have the same finite length; a chain is saturated if no additional prime can be inserted between successive terms. The ideal $\sqrt{(0)}$ consists of the nilpotent elements of $C$.

proof.text: By [lem-exc-fields-excellent], the given field $k$ is excellent. This applies to every characteristic and does not require $k$ to be perfect.

Apply [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent] with $R=k$, $E=B$, and $M=B\setminus\mathfrak p$. The finite-generation hypothesis is exactly the hypothesis on $B$. Primality makes $M$ multiplicatively closed and ensures $1\in M$. By [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], the localization in its conclusion is $L=B_{\mathfrak p}$, so $L$ is excellent and is a local ring.

Excellence includes Noetherianity by [def-exc-excellent-ring], so $L$ is Noetherian. Apply the forward implication of [lem-sc-strict-henselization-noetherian] to the strict henselization $C$ relative to the chosen separable closure $K$. It gives that $C$ is Noetherian. The local-ring hypothesis is supplied by the localization in step 2; no finite residue-extension hypothesis is needed.

By [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization], $C$ is isomorphic as an $L$-algebra to the colimit of the pointed etale $L$-algebras $(S,\chi:S\to K)$. The objects and morphisms here are exactly those in [lem-sc-pointed-etale-small-filtered]: an object of its full subcategory of $\operatorname{Over}(\operatorname{CommAlgCat}_L(K))$ is such a map $\chi$, and a morphism is an $L$-algebra map commuting with $\chi$. Consequently this category $P$ is essentially small and filtered. Choose a small full skeleton $J$ and, for each object $X$ of $P$, an isomorphism $u_X:rX\to X$ from its representative, with $u_X$ the identity on representatives. A finite diagram in $J$ has a cocone in $P$ by filteredness; composing its legs with the inverse of the chosen isomorphism of its vertex gives a cocone in $J$, so $J$ is filtered. A cocone $(\lambda_j)$ on the restricted algebra diagram extends by $\lambda_X=\lambda_{rX}\circ u_X^{-1}$; for a morphism $f:X\to Y$, its naturality follows by applying the restricted cocone identity to $u_Y^{-1}fu_X:rX\to rY$. Restriction and extension are inverse, also on morphisms of cocones. Thus $C$ with its transported cocone is the colimit of the small filtered diagram. Each term $S$ is etale over $L$ by its definition, and clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-finite-presentation-localization] gives its finite presentation over $L$. This very presentation satisfies [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra], proving that $L\to C$ is ind-etale.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability], an ind-etale map is weakly etale, so $L\to C$ is weakly etale. Apply [lem-exc-weakly-etale-excellent] to this map. Its excellent-source hypothesis was proved in step 2, and its Noetherian-target hypothesis in step 3. The conclusion is that $C$ is excellent.

proof.text: Let $I$ be any ideal of $C$. The scalar homomorphism $C\to C/I$ is surjective, so every element of $C/I$ is already a scalar and the empty finite list generates it as a $C$-algebra. Apply the final sentence of [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent] with $R=C$ and $A=C/I$. Its excellent-source hypothesis is step 5, and the preceding finite-generation argument supplies its finite-type hypothesis. It gives that $C/I$ is excellent directly. This applies also to $I=(0)$ and $I=C$; no properness or finite-generation hypothesis on $I$ is used.

source.place: Tag 07QU (lemma-finite-type-over-excellent), finite-type specialization applied directly to the quotient algebra.

proof.text: By [def-exc-excellent-ring], the excellence of $C$ includes its Noetherianity. The nilpotent elements form an ideal: if $x^a=0$ and $y^b=0$ for positive integers $a,b$, the binomial expansion makes $(x+y)^{a+b}=0$, and $(-x)^a=0$ and $(rx)^a=0$ for every $r$. Hence $\sqrt{(0)}$ is an allowed ideal in step 6. That step gives excellence of $C/\sqrt{(0)}$, and unfolding excellence again gives its Noetherianity.
